internship-guidelines:
**Internship Guidelines**, A set of rules and best practices that students must follow while completing their internship for CSC462.

## Key points
- **Eligibility**: Minimum 3.0 GPA, completed core CS courses, and signed a consent form.  
- **Duration**: 12 weeks of full-time work, with a 2-hour weekly progress report.  
- **Supervisor Agreement**: Company supervisor must provide a written scope of work and a mentor sign-off.  
- **Academic Credit**: 3 credits awarded upon submission of a final report and a supervisor evaluation.  
- **Professional Conduct**: Students must adhere to the university code of ethics, maintain confidentiality, and report any workplace violations.  
- **Evaluation**: Assessment based on project deliverables, attendance, and a final presentation to the faculty panel.

## Example  
```text
Week 1: Orientation, set up development environment, meet team.
Week 2-4: Design phase, create UML diagrams, write functional spec.
Week 5-8: Implementation, code modules, unit test, integrate.
Week 9-10: QA, perform regression tests, fix bugs.
Week 11: Prepare final report, introduction, methodology, results, conclusion.
Week 12: Deliver presentation, 15-minute talk, Q&A with faculty panel.
```

## Exam focus  
1. **What is the minimum GPA required for internship eligibility?**  
   *Answer: 3.0.*

2. **How many credits are awarded for completing the internship?**  
   *Answer: 3 credits.*

Students should be able to relate and contextualize the above-mentioned concepts with their project work/activities done during internship at the host organization.

Citation and Referencing

The listing of references should be listed in the references section. The references contain the list of articles, books, URLs that are cited in the document. The books, articles, and others that are studied during the study but are not cited in the document can be listed in the bibliography section. The citation and referencing standard should be APA referencing standard. The text inside the document should be cited accordingly. The APA referencing standard can be found in the web at https://apastyle.apa.org/

Report Format Standards

A. Page Number

The pages from certificate page to the list of tables/figures/abbreviations/approvals should be numbered in roman starting from i. The pages from chapter 1 onwards should be numbered in numeric starting from 1. The page number should be inserted at bottom, aligned center.

B. Page Size and Margin

• The paper size must be a page size corresponding to A4. The margins must be set as

Top = 1; Bottom = 1; Right = 1; Left 1.25

C. Paragraph Style

• All paragraphs must be justified and have spacing of 1.5.

D. Text Font of Document

• The contents in the document should be in Times New Roman font

• The font size in the paragraphs of document should be 12

E. Section Headings

• Font size for the headings should be 16 for chapter headings, 14 for section headings, 12 for sub-section headings. All the headings should be bold faced.

F. Figures and Tables

• Position of figures and tables should be aligned center. The figure caption should be centred below the figure and table captions should be centred above the table. All the captions should be of bold face with 12 font size.

Final Report Binding and Submissio n:

No of Copies: 3 (College Library + Self + Dean Office) Look and Feel: Golden Embracing with Black Binding A final approved signed copy of the report should be submitted to the Dean Office, Exam Section, Institute of Science and Technology, Tribhuvan University
internship-report-sample:
**Definition**  
An internship report sample is a template that demonstrates the structure, content, and formatting required for a student’s internship report in CSC462.

## Key points
- **Structure**: Title page, abstract, table of contents, introduction, company profile, internship objectives, tasks performed, learning outcomes, challenges, conclusions, references, appendices.  
- **Content depth**: Each section must contain concise, factual information; avoid vague statements.  
- **Formatting**: Use 12-point Times New Roman, 1.5 line spacing, 1-inch margins, numbered pages.  
- **Documentation**: Include screenshots, code snippets, and data tables where relevant.  
- **Evaluation criteria**: Clarity of objectives, relevance of tasks, critical reflection, and professional presentation.

## Example (excerpt)

```text
Title: Internship Report, Software Development at XYZ Corp
Author: A. B. Student
Date: 15 March 2024

Abstract
This report documents the internship experience at XYZ Corp, focusing on the development of a RESTful API for inventory management. The internship lasted 12 weeks, during which I designed, implemented, and tested the API using Spring Boot and PostgreSQL.

Table of Contents
1. Introduction
2. Company Profile
3. Internship Objectives
4. Tasks Performed
   4.1 Requirement Analysis
   4.2 API Design
   4.3 Implementation
   4.4 Testing
5. Learning Outcomes
6. Challenges and Solutions
7. Conclusion
8. References
9. Appendices

...

Appendix A, Sample Code
```java

public class InventoryController {

    @Autowired
    private InventoryService service;

    @GetMapping("/{id}")
    public ResponseEntity<Item> getItem(@PathVariable Long id) {
        return ResponseEntity.ok(service.findById(id));
    }
}
```
```

## Exam focus
1. **What are the mandatory sections of a CSC462 internship report?**  
   *Answer: Title page, abstract, table of contents, introduction, company profile, internship objectives, tasks performed, learning outcomes, challenges, conclusions, references, appendices.*

2. **Which formatting style must be used for the report?**  
   *Answer: 12-point Times New Roman, 1.5 line spacing, 1-inch margins, numbered pages.*
internship-sample-presentation:
**Definition**  
An Internship Sample Presentation is a structured oral or visual demonstration that interns deliver to showcase their project work, learning outcomes, and professional skills during the internship period.

## Key points
- **Structure**: Introduction, objectives, methodology, results, challenges, lessons learned, and future work.  
- **Content**: Focus on the internship project, not the entire internship experience.  
- **Audience**: Typically faculty, internship supervisors, and peers.  
- **Visual aids**: Slides, charts, code snippets, or live demos; keep them clear and concise.  
- **Timing**: 10, 15 minutes of speaking time, followed by 5 minutes of Q&A.  
- **Evaluation criteria**: Clarity, depth of analysis, relevance to course objectives, and professionalism.

## Example  
```text
Slide 1: Title, “Automated Email Classification Using Naïve Bayes”
Slide 2: Objective, Reduce spam by 30% for the university mail system
Slide 3: Methodology, Data collection (10,000 emails), preprocessing (tokenization, stop-word removal), model training (scikit-learn)
Slide 4: Results, Accuracy 92%, Precision 90%, Recall 88%
Slide 5: Challenges, Imbalanced dataset, limited computational resources
Slide 6: Lessons Learned, Importance of feature engineering, need for continuous evaluation
Slide 7: Future Work, Deploy model on cloud, integrate with existing mail server
```

## Exam focus  
1. **What are the essential sections of an internship sample presentation?**  
   *Answer:* Introduction, objectives, methodology, results, challenges, lessons learned, and future work.  

2. **Why is a 10, 15 minute speaking time recommended for the presentation?**  
   *Answer:* It allows concise delivery of key points while leaving time for questions and maintaining audience engagement.
